style.a: Idempotency means that sending the same request multiple times produces the same final state as sending it once, without accumulating side effects. A GET request is idempotent by design, while a POST that creates a resource must be idempotent only if the client includes an idempotency key and the server rejects duplicates instead of creating them twice. Idempotency protects against retries and network failures, but it does not make every HTTP method idempotent by default.

Python threads share the global interpreter lock, so CPU-bound work is not automatically parallel across cores. Multiprocessing spawns separate processes, each with its own interpreter and memory, and can use all available cores. The trade-off is interprocess communication and serialization, which can add overhead. Multiprocessing is therefore useful for CPU-bound tasks, while threads remain preferable for I/O-bound work.
